dedupe_keys.name: 30 m global impervious surface area dynamics and urban expansion pattern observed by landsat satellites from 1972 to 2019

description: Wuhan University and Sun Yat-Sen University publish GISA, a global impervious-surface history derived from more than three million Landsat images. The product covers 1972–2019 at thirty-metre resolution across global land, not only inside a predefined urban mask. Zenodo distributes tiled GeoTIFF files publicly and free under CC-BY-4.0. The producer reports evaluation using 120,777 reference sites across 270 cities, with an F-score of 0.954. Those aggregate results do not establish equal performance in every location or year, especially where early imagery is sparse. This uncertainty matters when deriving urban runoff coefficients or comparing small local changes. The grids can represent paved and built surfaces in drainage, heat and urban-expansion simulations. They complement building-footprint inventories with impervious land beyond individual structures and with earlier historical coverage. No validation samples or rasters were downloaded.
